newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Gold loses lustre, still ornamental.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Gold loses lustre, still ornamental.

text.p: Gold has lost much of its lustre among professional investors but retains its appeal as an object of desire among consumers, a leading gold analyst said on Wednesday.

"Over the longer time frame, people have lost interest in gold as a pure investment because there has been no inflation in the system," Stewart Murray of Gold Fields Mineral Services Ltd said in an interview.

This disillusionment is reflected in current prices, which have been hovering around three or four year lows. Gold has long been perceived as an investment of choice in times of inflation concerns as a hedge against less tangible paper investments.
But while Wall Street may be shying from gold, not so jewellery makers, who last year were busier than ever.
Stewart said this year more gold jewellery will be made than ever before, although the growth in gold jewellery fabrication has slowed a bit since the 1980s.
"We probably saw record levels of jewellery fabrication last year," Murray said.
Still, signs are emerging that the appetite for gold jewellery in China that has accompanied rapid economic growth is waning, Stewart said.
"What we've seen in the last year is China slowing down," Stewart said.
This has a ripple effect on other Asian countries, which supply China with jewellery, he said.
Also, unlike India, where gold is much revered and imbedded in the social fabric, China's love of gold is less intense.
"They haven't got the same affinity the Indians have got," Stewart said.
Indeed, other objects of desire, such as precious gems, have caught the sparkle of China's newly affluent.
"A lot of people are buying gem-set jewellery," Stewart said. "The price you pay goes for the rock not for the gold."
As far as professional investment in gold, equities and bond prices need to go into reverse to ignite the gold price, Murray said.
Otherwise, gold is destined to trade in a familar range for some time, he added.
